cards.front: Substance use in pregnancy requires a non-judgemental approach with harm reduction; abrupt cessation of opioids or benzodiazepines is [___].
cards.context:
Abrupt opioid cessation in pregnancy precipitates withdrawal in mother and fetus, risking fetal distress and preterm labour. Abrupt benzo cessation risks maternal seizures.

Frame as non-judgemental harm reduction — women who feel judged stop attending antenatal care.

cards.front: Vitamin K prophylaxis: preferred IM dose [___] mg at birth; if declined, oral regimen is three doses over 4 weeks.
cards.context:
VKDB (formerly HDN) affects neonates because the liver doesn't synthesise factors II, VII, IX, X without vitamin K, and breast milk has minimal vitamin K.

IM vitamin K 1 mg at birth — single-dose, near-100% effective, no compliance issues.

cards.front: Strongest single risk factor for developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH) is [___] presentation; other risks include female sex, family history, and oligohydramnios.
cards.context:
Breech position, female sex, family history and oligohydramnios increase DDH risk ([meta-analysis](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39853978/)).

Prematurity alone is not an established risk factor ([review](https://doi.org/10.1186/s12887-023-04083-1)).

cards.front: Mastitis treatment: continue [___] from affected side + flucloxacillin for Staph aureus coverage; abscess if fluctuant mass develops.
cards.context:
Mastitis is bacterial breast infection, almost always Staph aureus seeded through cracked nipples or milk duct stasis.

Antibiotics: flucloxacillin 500 mg four times daily (QID) for 5-7 days (cephalexin/clindamycin if pen allergic); analgesia + warm compresses.

Distinguish from engorgement (bilateral, no fever) and cracked nipples alone (visible cracks, painful latch).

cards.front: Obstetric VTE risk is assessed with a structured risk tool at booking, on admission to labour ward, and [___].
cards.context:
Assess obstetric VTE risk at booking, admission to labour ward and postpartum. Use the locally agreed risk tool and its phase thresholds; no scoring system has been prospectively validated in pregnancy.

Previous VTE and thrombophilia follow separate pathways; document the score and follow the local protocol.

Prophylaxis dose and duration depend on indication, weight, renal function and risk phase; extend postpartum prophylaxis for high-risk patients.

cards.front: The strongest combined risk factor for placenta accreta spectrum is placenta praevia overlying a prior [___] scar.
cards.context:
The decidua is deficient over a uterine scar, so a low-lying placenta implants abnormally into it.

Praevia over a previous C-section scar is the highest-risk combination; risk climbs with each prior C-section (≈3% → 11% → 40% → 61%).

cards.front: Endometriosis work-up uses pelvic USS or MRI; consider [___] when imaging is negative and empirical treatment is unsuccessful or inappropriate.
cards.context:
Use pelvic ultrasound or MRI in the diagnostic work-up for endometriosis, while recognising that negative imaging does not exclude superficial peritoneal disease.

Consider laparoscopy when imaging is negative and empirical treatment is unsuccessful or inappropriate; when lesions are sampled at laparoscopy, histology helps confirm the diagnosis. CA-125 is non-specific.

Modern practice: empirical medical therapy first (NSAIDs + continuous COC/progestin → dienogest → GnRH agonists with add-back HRT); laparoscopy for diagnostic uncertainty, treatment failure, or fertility concerns.

cards.front: Chorionicity in twins must be determined by 14 weeks; lambda sign indicates [___], T sign indicates MCDA.
cards.context:
Lambda (λ) sign = a triangular wedge of placental tissue pushing into the base of the dividing membrane → dichorionic (DCDA).

T sign = the membrane meets the placenta at a right angle with no wedge of tissue → monochorionic (MCDA). Both are reliable ONLY in the first trimester (thick membrane, visible placental insertion).

Mis-classification matters: MCDA share one placenta — 2-weekly scans from 16 weeks (TTTS 10-15%, TAPS, selective FGR); DCDA need 4-weekly from 20 weeks.

cards.front: While preparing for caesarean in umbilical cord prolapse, placing the woman in the [___] position lets gravity keep the presenting part off the cord.
cards.context:
Cord prolapse threatens the fetus through cord compression.

Buy time by elevating the presenting part off the cord (hand or knee-chest/Trendelenburg position) and minimising cord handling, while preparing for immediate delivery — usually category-1 caesarean.

cards.front: Normal pregnancy arterial blood gas (ABG) shows a chronic compensated respiratory alkalosis with PaCO₂ around [___] mmHg and HCO₃⁻ around 18-22 mmol/L.
cards.context: The driver is progesterone, which acts on the central respiratory chemoreceptors to raise tidal volume by ~40% (rate is unchanged). The kidneys then excrete bicarbonate to keep pH near the upper limit of normal.

cards.front: Group B streptococcus (GBS)-positive women receive intrapartum IV benzylpenicillin in labour to prevent neonatal sepsis; ideally given at least [___] hours before delivery.
cards.context:
GBS colonises the lower genital tract in 20-30% of women asymptomatically; vertical transmission during birth → early-onset neonatal GBS disease (sepsis, pneumonia, meningitis) in the first week.

Intrapartum IV benzylpenicillin (3 g load, then 1.8 g every 4 h until delivery) prevents this. Routine vaginal-rectal GBS swab at 35-37 weeks; positive → intrapartum antibiotics.

If GBS status unknown in labour, treat empirically if: preterm <37 weeks, ROM ≥18 h, intrapartum fever ≥38°C, previous GBS baby, or GBS bacteriuria.

cards.front: In IUGR, absent or reversed end-diastolic flow in the umbilical artery Doppler indicates severe placental insufficiency and warrants considering [___].
cards.context:
Umbilical artery Doppler worsens with placental insufficiency: normal → raised resistance (UA-PI above the 95th centile) → absent end-diastolic flow (AEDF) → reversed end-diastolic flow (REDF).

NSW Health (GL2025_018) plans birth for reversed flow from 30 weeks and absent flow from 32 weeks. Before 30 weeks, an absent or reversed ductus venosus a-wave triggers birth planning.

A low MCA pulsatility index (brain-sparing) or a cerebroplacental ratio below 1 calls for at least weekly Doppler surveillance, but is not itself a trigger for birth.

cards.front: Physiological anaemia of pregnancy stays [___] on the film, so a falling mean cell volume instead points to superimposed iron deficiency.
cards.context:
The trap is calling every low third-trimester haemoglobin 'iron deficiency'.

Pure haemodilution does not change red-cell size, so normal indices with ferritin >30 µg/L are expected; a dropping MCV or ferritin <30 µg/L means true deficiency has been superimposed and needs treatment.

cards.front: At 31 weeks, a woman treated for hypertension since before pregnancy develops new proteinuria and persistent visual disturbance. Her booking urine was normal. These findings change the diagnosis to [___].
cards.context:
New proteinuria and neurological symptoms after 20 weeks indicate disease added to the pre-existing hypertension.

A blood-pressure rise alone can reflect worsening chronic hypertension; the new systemic features are the discriminator here.

cards.front: Milk production is driven by prolactin, while milk ejection (let-down) is driven by [___].
cards.context: Two hormones, two jobs: prolactin drives milk PRODUCTION, while oxytocin drives milk EJECTION (let-down) by contracting myoepithelial cells. Suckling stimulates both; oxytocin also helps the uterus involute.

cards.front: Transvaginal cervical length ≤[___] mm at 16-24 weeks defines a 'short cervix' and substantially raises spontaneous preterm birth risk.
cards.context:
Use transvaginal ultrasound to confirm suspected short cervix. In the current WA pathway, low-risk screening starts with transabdominal assessment at the 18-20-week anatomy scan.

If transabdominal length is under 35 mm, confirm transvaginally. A confirmed 21-25 mm prompts vaginal progesterone and repeat scanning; shorter measurements need specialist review.

cards.front: PCOS Rotterdam criteria require 2 of 3: oligo/anovulation, [___] (clinical or biochemical), and polycystic ovaries on USS.
cards.context:
PCOS = 2 of 3 Rotterdam criteria: oligo/anovulation, hyperandrogenism (hirsutism, acne, alopecia, OR raised free testosterone), polycystic ovaries on USS (≥20 follicles per ovary or volume >10 mL).

Downstream risks: endometrial hyperplasia + cancer from unopposed estrogen (cyclic progestogen if anovulatory), insulin resistance + T2DM, CV disease, and subfertility (letrozole first-line).

Assess glycaemic status at diagnosis and repeat every 1-3 years according to diabetes risk. A 75-g OGTT is the most accurate test; fasting glucose or HbA1c are less accurate alternatives when an OGTT cannot be performed.

cards.front: HPV vaccination prevents about 90% of cervical cancers; cervical [___] is still required because the vaccine misses the remaining oncogenic HPV types.
cards.context:
The nonavalent vaccine covers seven oncogenic types (16, 18, 31, 33, 45, 52, 58) plus the low-risk wart types 6 and 11.

Vaccinated women therefore still need screening to catch the residual risk.

The National Cervical Screening Program runs 5-yearly HPV testing from 25 to 74 regardless of vaccination; any oncogenic HPV gets reflex liquid-based cytology, and HPV 16/18 goes to colposcopy.

cards.front: Between 24 and 36 weeks, symphysis-fundal height normally rises by about [___] per week.
cards.context:
The trend across visits matters more than any single reading, because one tape measurement varies between examiners.

Over four weeks, expect roughly 4 cm of growth. A rise of only 1 cm in four weeks is slower than this rough rule and needs assessment.
